ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \triangle ABC$ is inscribed in $ \odot O$, $ \angle ABC>90^\circ$. The bisector of its exterior angle $ \angle EAC$ intersects $ \odot O$ at point D. Connect $ DB, DC$, where $ DB$ intersects $ AC$ at point F. Given $ DB=DC$ and $ DA=DF$, when $ \angle ABC=\alpha $, find the measure of $ \angle DFC$ in degrees (expressed in an algebraic formula involving $ \alpha$)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $DA=DF$,\\
it follows that $\angle DAF=\angle DFA$,\\
hence, $\angle DAF=\angle DFA=\angle CBD=\angle BCD$,\\
therefore, $\triangle DAF\sim \triangle DBC$,\\
which means that $\angle ADF=\angle BDC$,\\
given that $\angle ABC=\alpha$ and knowing that the opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary,\\
it follows that $\angle ADC=180^\circ-\alpha$,\\
thus, $\angle ADF=90^\circ-\frac{\alpha}{2}$,\\
resulting in $\angle DAF=\angle DFA=\left(180^\circ-\angle ADF\right)\div 2=45^\circ+\frac{\alpha}{4}$,\\
therefore, $\angle DFC=180^\circ-\angle DFA=\boxed{135^\circ-\frac{\alpha}{4}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a circle with points A, B, C, and D on the circumference. Point O is inside the circle. Segment DB crosses segment AC at an interior point labeled F. Segments DA, DC, DB, BC, AC, and AB are drawn, and an exterior ray AE is drawn at A, matching the statement that D is related to the exterior angle at A. The target angle ∠DFC is formed by FD along DB and FC along AC. Reasoning: Since DA = DF, triangle DAF is isosceles, so ∠DAF = ∠DFA. Because F lies on AC, ray AF is the same as ray AC, hence ∠DAF = ∠DAC. Since A, B, C, D are concyclic, ∠DAC and ∠DBC subtend the same chord DC, so ∠DAC = ∠DBC. Also DB = DC, so triangle DBC is isosceles and ∠DBC = ∠BCD. Therefore ∠DAF = ∠DFA = ∠DBC = ∠BCD, giving triangle DAF similar to triangle DBC. Thus the remaining corresponding angles are equal: ∠ADF = ∠BDC. From the diagram, F lies on DB, so ray DF is along DB. Therefore ∠ADC is split by DF into ∠ADF + ∠FDC, and ∠FDC = ∠BDC. Since ∠ADF = ∠BDC, we get ∠ADC = 2∠ADF. In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠ADC = 180° − ∠ABC = 180° − α. Hence ∠ADF = (180° − α)/2 = 90° − α/2. In isosceles triangle DAF, ∠DFA = (180° − ∠ADF)/2 = (180° − (90° − α/2))/2 = 45° + α/4. Since A, F, C are collinear, ∠DFC is supplementary to ∠DFA. Therefore ∠DFC = 180° − (45° + α/4) = 135° − α/4.
